'''Jacqui Ramagge''' is an English-Australian 
mathematician. She is Deputy Vice Chancellor at [[James Cook University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=University Executive - About JCU |url=https://www.jcu.edu.au/about-jcu/university-executive |website=www.jcu.edu.au |language=en-AU |date=18 February 2026}}</ref> She was previously the executive dean of [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] at the [[University of South Australia]].<ref name=unisa/> She was born in London, and emigrated to Australia in 1991.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|author-link=University of Wollongong|title=Biographies|url=https://documents.uow.edu.au/content/groups/public/@web/@inf/@math/documents/doc/uow052120.pdf}}</ref>

She is a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of New South Wales]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Fellows of the Royal Society of NSW: Jacqui Ramagge|url=https://www.royalsoc.org.au/images/fellows-pages/RSN-R-Fellows.html#fellow-ramagge-jacqui|access-date=2021-03-10|website=www.royalsoc.org.au}}</ref> and was the President of the [[Australian Mathematical Society]] (AustMS) from 2019 to 2020.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Office Bearers|url=https://austms.org.au/about-us/office-bearers/|access-date=2021-03-10|website=Australian Mathematical Society|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Ramagge was born in London into a family of Spanish immigrants. Consequently, her first language is Spanish and her native language is English. Her school years were spent first at Hallfield Primary School and later at Holland Park Comprehensive School. Until the age of 18 all her summers were spent in a village in northern Spain. Ramagge was the first person in her family to go to university.<ref name=":4" />

Ramagge studied at the [[University of Warwick]], where she obtained a BA (First Class) in mathematics in 1988, an MSc in mathematics in 1990, and a PhD in 1993.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Jacqui Ramagge|url=http://www.jacquiramagge.com/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225132145/http://www.jacquiramagge.com/|archive-date=2021-02-25|url-status=dead|website=www.jacquiramagge.com}}</ref> During her PhD, Ramagge won the 1993 [[B. H. Neumann Prize]] for the most outstanding talk presented by a student at the Annual Meeting of the [[AustMS]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=The Bernhard Neumann Prize|url=https://austms.org.au/awards-grants/awards/the-bernhard-neumann-prize/|access-date=2021-03-10|website=Australian Mathematical Society|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
From 1993 to 2007, Ramagge worked as an academic at the [[University of Newcastle (Australia)|University of Newcastle]]. In 2005, she was the Assistant Dean of Marketing and Recruitment in the Faculty of Science and IT<ref name=":3" /> and she was Director of the Women@UoN program in 2006, providing professional development of both academic and professional staff at the University of Newcastle.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jacqui Ramagge|url=https://www.chelseadigital.ca/Jacqui/Qualifications.html|access-date=2021-05-10|website=www.chelseadigital.ca|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510040608/https://www.chelseadigital.ca/Jacqui/Qualifications.html|archive-date=2021-05-10|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From 2007 to 2015, Ramagge was an academic at the [[University of Wollongong]]. She was Director of the Australian Mathematical Science Institute Summer School held there over the summer of 2008—2009 and served as the Head of School of Mathematics and Applied Statistics 2009–2015.<ref name=":3" />

Ramagge was appointed as Professor of Mathematics at the University of Sydney in 2015,<ref name=":3" /> making her the second woman Professor of Mathematics in the history of the institution,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|last=Singhal|first=Pallavi|date=2018-11-12|title=Sydney University launches $6.5 million Global Mathematics Institute|url=https://www.smh.com.au/education/sydney-university-launches-6-5-million-global-mathematics-institute-20181112-p50fgk.html|access-date=2021-05-10|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en}}</ref> the first having been Professor [[Nalini Joshi]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Australia|first=Women in STEMM|date=2019-05-10|title=To maths or not to maths? That is the question|url=https://womeninscienceaust.org/2019/05/10/to-maths-or-not-to-maths-that-is-the-question/|access-date=2021-05-10|website=Women in STEMM Australia|language=en-AU}}</ref> Ramagge was Head of School of Mathematics and Statistics from 2016–2019.<ref name=":3" /> During this time, she supported the establishment of the Sydney Mathematical Research Institute, working with Professor [[Geordie Williamson]] and Professor Anthony Henderson to raise $6.5 million of philanthropic donations from the Simon Marais Foundation, the Hooper Shaw Foundation and individuals to found the institute.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Global mathematics institute launched at the University of Sydney|url=https://www.sydney.edu.au/news-opinion/news/2018/11/12/global-mathematics-institute-launched-at-the-university-of-sydne.html|access-date=2021-03-10|website=The University of Sydney|language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-11-16|title=University of Sydney opens new mathematics research institute|url=https://www.abc.net.au/radionational/programs/scienceshow/university-of-sydney-opens-new-mathematics-research-institute/10505392|access-date=2021-05-10|website=ABC Radio National|language=en-AU}}</ref>

After a stint as executive dean of science at [[Durham University]] in the UK,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=About Durham University : Professor Jacqui Ramagge, Executive Dean (Science) – Durham University|url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/about/governance/senior/jramagge/|access-date=2021-03-10|website=www.dur.ac.uk}}</ref> Ramagge became executive dean of [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] at the [[University of South Australia]] in 2023.<ref name=unisa>{{cite web|url=https://unisa.edu.au/unisanews/2023/june/story6/|date=June 2023|title=Appointments: New Executive Dean to continue success in STEM|work=News from the University of South Australia: Achievements and Announcements|access-date=2025-12-21}}</ref>

== Research interests ==
Ramagge’s research interests overlap [[algebra]], analysis and [[geometry]]. Her current major projects focus on the general structure theory of totally disconnected, [[locally compact group]]s; and [[operator algebra]]s.<ref name=":3" />

In the field of totally disconnected, [[locally compact group]]s, Ramagge is driving the development of the geometric aspects of the theory. In [[operator algebra]]s, she works mainly on [[C*-algebra]]s, which were introduced to provide mathematical models for quantum mechanics, and in classifying their equilibrium states. Her work in functional analysis on buildings with Robertson and Steger provided insights into the Baum-Connes conjecture.<ref name=":3" />

Ramagge has published 28 research publications (correct of March 2021) in the areas of group theory, functional analysis, operator algebras, control theory, and statistical analyses of learning outcomes. She has received 10 [[Australian Research Council]] (ARC) grants since 2002.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|last=Council|first=Australian Research|date=2018-06-29|title=Archived ERA Reports|url=https://www.arc.gov.au/excellence-research-australia/archived-era-reports|access-date=2021-05-10|website=www.arc.gov.au|language=en}}</ref>

== Awards, honours and memberships ==
Ramagge became a Fellow of AustMS in 2014, having been closely involved with the Society since 1992. She was President Elect in 2018, President 2019–2020, and Immediate Past President in 2021 [4], continuing to serve as President after her return to the UK in 2020.<ref name=":2" /> She has been an Editor of the AustMS’s Lecture Series since 2011 and was Chief Editor from 2017–2019.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

Ramagge became a Fellow of the Royal Society of New South Wales in 2019.<ref name=":1" />

In 2013, Ramagge won the B. H. Neumann Award for Excellence in Mathematics Enrichment from the Australian Mathematics Trust, having served on the Primary Problems Committee since its inception in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BH Neumann Award Recipients|url=https://www.amt.edu.au/amt-awards|access-date=2021-03-10|website=Australian Maths Trust|language=en-AU|archive-date=25 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210325153152/https://www.amt.edu.au/amt-awards|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ramagge has also held the following memberships and leadership roles:<ref name=":3" />

* Chair of the Australian Council of Heads of Maths and Stats (2017–2018)
* Member of the Board of the Australian Mathematics Trust (2016—2020) 
* Member of the Mathematics, Information and Computing Sciences Research Evaluation Committee, Australian Research Council (ARC) Excellence for Research in Australia (2015, 2018)<ref name=":7" />
* Chair of the ARC [[Australian Laureate Fellowship]] Selection Advisory Committee (2014), Committee member (2012–2014)
* Member of University of Wollongong Council, the governing body of the institution (2013—2015)
* Member of the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (ACARA): Senior Secondary Mathematics Curriculum Advisory Panel (2012)
* Member of the [[Australian Academy of Science National Committees|Australian Academy of Science National Committee]] for the Mathematical Sciences (2011–2014, 2019–2020)
*  Member of ARC College of Experts, Engineering, Mathematics and Informatics Panel (2010–2012)
* [[Australian Mathematical Sciences Institute]] (AMSI) Educational Advisory Committee (2009---2019)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Governance|url=https://amsi.org.au/about-us/governance/|access-date=2021-05-10|website=AMSI|language=en-US}}</ref>
* Judge on the Committee for the AustMS B. H. Neumann Prize (1995–2005), seven times as Chair<ref name=":5" />
